engagement_title: Ridgeway Rovers kit refresh: recover a crest that survives only as stitching, rebuild the club's hand drawn numbering as cuttable artwork, and carry both onto twenty four signed off back of shirt sheets, a supplier spec and a committee board
vertical: Sports and recreation, grassroots amateur football, a village club near Cirencester in the English Cotswolds with two senior sides, a veterans XI and four junior age groups, printing through one local kit supplier
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork jersey numbering brief (cand_46, db_i 823), in which a custom football kit shop asks for its signature numbering rebuilt as clean, print ready vector artwork with consistent stroke widths and even spacing for heat transfer and flock production, worked up from photographed reference sheets as original geometry rather than lifted from a proprietary font file. The shop is laundered to a fictional village club, Ridgeway Rovers FC; no real club, competition, player, supplier or typeface is named. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com brief 'Realistic Textile Embroidery Design', quoted verbatim in the ledger ('a skilled embroidery designer to create a realistic logo. Requirements: Realism style, Medium size (3-6 inches)'), which pins the crest to an embroidered artefact at a small physical reproduction size rather than a flat scan, plus the companion candidate 'Premium Heritage Apparel Identity System & Factory-Ready Vector Engineering', whose framing is to translate an existing concept into factory ready vector engineering. The STRENGTHEN verdict keeps that concept and deliverable set; what the v3 audit adds is reach, since an ink level selection recovers a mark off a stitched surface, the supplier's own press PDF converts into a live merge template, and HTML authoring gives the spec and board as one native editable document.
client_one_liner: Our crest exists nowhere except stitched on last year's shirts, our numbers and letters were drawn by hand in the nineties on two sheets of graph paper, and the supplier needs everything by the end of the month.
client_brief:
Ridgeway Rovers FC, kit refresh for the coming season

We are a village club near Cirencester. Two senior sides, a veterans XI and four junior age groups. Everything we print goes through one local kit supplier, and this year we change shirts for the first time since 2019.

The crest. It exists on the shirts and nowhere else. When our old kit secretary moved away he took the artwork with him, and what we have is a photograph one of the parents took of the crest stitched on last season's home shirt. We need it back as proper artwork we can hand to any supplier: the crest as it is, a single ink version for the shirt breast and the training tops, and a version that works on the navy away shirt.

The numbering. Our numbers and letters were drawn by hand by a founding member in the nineties and they are genuinely ours, nobody else has them. Two sheets survive, one of the alphabet and one of the digits, both in marker on graph paper, both photographed on someone's kitchen table. We want them rebuilt as clean artwork with even, consistent strokes so the supplier can cut them.

The squad. Twenty four players. We need a back of shirt sheet per player showing their name and number, laid out the way the supplier's own sheet does it, one player per page, because the parents sign each one off before anything is cut. Last year's sheet from the supplier is attached and that is the format they want back.

We also need a sheet for the supplier showing the colours, the sizes and where things sit on the shirt, and a board showing the home and the away shirt with the crest on them, so the committee can see it before we commit the money.

Shirts are twenty eight to forty five dollars and the buyers are players and parents. It should look like a proper club, not a franchise and not a school project. And a note telling us anything we ought to know.
price_band_and_audience: Grassroots kit at 28 to 45 dollars a shirt, bought by players and by parents paying for a child's fourth kit in five years. The band is load bearing in the artwork itself: at this price the supplier cuts numbering as one robust spot colour in heat press vinyl or flock, so the glyphs must reduce to a single solid generously weighted closed geometry with no thin joins, no inline, no outline and no second colour. A pro tier sublimated number with a keyline and a gradient is not merely expensive here, it is uncuttable and the supplier bounces it. Push the other way into clip art blockiness and a club whose crest has been stitched on shirts since 1974 looks supermarket rebranded. The same tension runs through the crest, since holding as one ink at shirt breast size is a different drawing decision from a full colour crest that only appears large. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.values: Keeping what is genuinely theirs, the 1974 crest and the founder's numbering, and reading as a real village club rather than a franchise or a school project.

assets_supplied.name: ridgeway_crest_shirt.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld phone photograph of the club crest embroidered on the breast of last season's home shirt, laid flat on a kitchen table under a ceiling light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the crest still exists. One of the parents took this off last year's shirt."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A compound lockup on stitched, non flat cloth: a ring of small caps lettering, a hairline rule inside it, a shield, and a ram's head inside the shield. One selection naming the crest as a single thing returns the ring and the shield outline while silently dropping the rule and the ram's head, naming the garment pulls the selection to the cloth, background removal on the enclosed ring hands back a solid opaque disc, and the right third sits in a fold shadow where navy thread and claret cloth run close in value.

assets_supplied.name: ridgeway_letters_sheet.jpg and ridgeway_numbers_sheet.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Two photographs of hand drawn reference sheets, one carrying the alphabet and one the digits zero to nine, drawn in marker on gridded graph paper and shot on a table.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our letters and our numbers, drawn by one of the founders. Two sheets, both photographed at home."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The sheets were drawn about a decade apart with different pens: the digits are monoline and the letters carry a modulated chisel stroke that thickens visibly at every join, and neither sheet declares it. The graph rule is printed pale blue and is dark enough to survive a trace as its own geometry, the alphabet sheet draws O twice and omits Q, and there is no apostrophe anywhere on either sheet.

assets_supplied.name: ridgeway_shirtback_2024.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The supplier's back of shirt sheet from last season, a genuine press PDF from their own studio, one player per page, carrying name, number, initial, size and a small crest.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The format our supplier wants. This is last year's, with last year's captain on it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The readout of the converted document's editable text is lossy: it omits one run while keeping that run's line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator still reports the mapping valid with no warnings and the placeholder build still reports success. It also carries no bleed, and bleed cannot be introduced into a document derived this way.

assets_supplied.name: ridgeway_squad.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twenty four rows: first name, surname, shirt number, age group and shirt size, as registered with the county association.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The squad as registered. The secretary allocated the numbers."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two brothers share the surname Halloway and the supplier's own rule needs an initial in front of a repeated surname, the number 14 appears on two rows, and one surname (Featherstonehaugh) is long enough that a fixed measure frame stops rendering it at the frame edge rather than spilling or warning. One player is O'Dwyer, whose apostrophe exists on neither drawn sheet.

assets_supplied.name: ridgeway_shirt_blanks.jpg (2 frames, 12 megapixel)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs of the two blank shirts from the supplier, home in claret and away in navy, each laid on a table.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The blanks the supplier sent. Home is claret, away is navy."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Shot on different evenings under a warm kitchen light, so the navy reads purple, the claret reads orange, and the two do not agree with each other. Both are twelve megapixel phone frames, well under the scale the committee board needs to judge a crest at, and nothing available can put pixels back.

assets_supplied.name: ridgeway_supplier_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the kit supplier: inks they can run, cut and heat press constraints, placement heights and the deadline.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the supplier told us they can actually do."

acceptance_bar: The crest is placeable artwork rather than a picture of a crest: scalable, a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath, delivered as the crest, a single ink version and a version that holds on navy.
Every element that is on the shirt is on the recovered crest. A crest that is recognisable but missing an interior element is not the crest.
The crest still reads at the size it reproduces on the shirt breast, not only at full canvas.
Thirty six glyphs are delivered, and the letters and the digits read as ONE set when a name sits above a number at back of shirt proportion.
No glyph carries the graph rule, a stray blue path or an unclosed counter, and every glyph is a single closed spot colour shape the supplier can cut.
Anything the drawn sheets cannot supply for this squad is named in writing rather than substituted silently.
Twenty four back of shirt pages exist, one player per page, with every field the supplier's sheet carries populated on every page.
Each player's full name renders complete on their own page. A name that stops at the frame edge fails even though the page count is right.
The proof that carries a player's name is that player's proof. A proof named for one player showing another is a rejected sheet, not a filing error.
No delivered raster exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from.

The spec and both boards arrive as ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, crest as live vector shapes, words as retypable text, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
On BOTH the home and away board the applied number reads as printed on the shirt rather than as a flat shape laid over a photograph.
One type system across the spec and both boards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.
The note states what was recovered, what was rebuilt, every reconciliation against the squad list, and anything the club should know before handing this to a second supplier.

adobe_surfaces.role: Every recovery decision: lifting the crest off stitched cloth at thread level rather than garment level, separating drawn marker strokes from a printed graph rule so the trace does not inherit the paper, preparing each glyph raster (the only lever tracing responds to), performing the vector hygiene the trace does not do, and bringing two badly lit blank shirt frames toward one target.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and data merge, driven from the supplier's own press PDF
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (readout and validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution)
adobe_surfaces.role: The twenty four back of shirt sheets as a genuine record per page run reverse engineered from a flat supplier PDF with no native file supplied. It is the only surface here producing one record per page at volume, it is where the recovered crest and rebuilt glyphs are finally seen at true proportion, and it is where the parent facing proofs come from.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview

Photographs must be inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the crest and glyph specimen go in as inline SVG to stay editable vector, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url

The recommender refuses to pair by design so the pairing is the agent's art direction, numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, and every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the club cannot supply, a plain garment shot at camera scale so the board can show the crest at the size the committee has to judge it at, IP clean with generative candidates excluded. Boards persists the sign off set within the twelve per call cap, with partial success read as partial and vector unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and decide which deliverable belongs on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: Twenty four sheets in the supplier's format at one player per page is a record per page run; the spec and boards are collateral the club must edit later, which only authored fixed canvas layout gives. The brief pins both, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which sheet.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at everything before deciding anything: the crest frame, both drawn sheets, both blank shirt frames, and the squad list read against what the sheets actually contain.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts an alphabet and a set of digits. Only the sheets can settle whether the squad's names are spellable from them, and counting cells is not reading them. The two blanks must be judged against each other, not each alone.
trajectory.produces: A triage note on crest condition, sheet character, blank illuminants and a first name to glyph reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Straighten the two drawn sheets and the crest frame where they sit off level, before any crop or bounds decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels so it cannot follow a crop, and a glyph traced off a rotated sheet carries the rotation into the cut file.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Select the crest off the shirt by naming the stitching's own visual properties rather than the garment, set polarity for tracing, and crop to the selection's returned bounds.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate: naming the shirt pulls the selection to the cloth. The fold shadow side has almost no separation, so the right of the crest is not guaranteed to behave like the left, and background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring.
trajectory.produces: A crest plate at native scale with its selection bounds recorded.

trajectory.action: Trace the crest plate, inject a viewBox, remove the opaque full canvas ground path, and derive the single ink and reversed variants.
trajectory.judgement: Tracing takes no options at all, so everything is decided in the raster prep. The single ink version is a different drawing decision from a reduction, because elements that survive by colour separation alone stop working at shirt breast size in one colour.
trajectory.produces: A crest as scalable transparent geometry plus single ink and reversed derivatives.

trajectory.action: Separate the drawn marker strokes on each sheet from the printed graph rule, one sheet at a time, and prepare each raster so the strokes are solid and closed.
trajectory.judgement: The graph rule is dark enough to become geometry. Selecting the ink by its own colour and medium rather than by the paper keeps the grid out, and the raster prep is the only lever the trace responds to.
trajectory.produces: Two clean glyph rasters carrying strokes and nothing else.

trajectory.action: Trace both sheets, hygiene each glyph, and lay a sample name above a sample number at back of shirt proportion to judge the set as a set.
trajectory.judgement: Thirty six glyphs that each look right individually are not a set. A set is judged only where a name sits above a number at the proportion the shirt uses, which is also where a cutter's tolerance is judged.
trajectory.produces: A thirty six glyph vector set with a proportion test of the pairing.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the finished glyph set against every surname and initial the squad list needs, and write down what the sheets cannot supply.
trajectory.judgement: The club believes it has an alphabet; what it has is what was drawn. Naming a gap in writing is a deliverable, inventing a glyph in the founder's hand is not the commission and is not honest.
trajectory.produces: A reconciliation of squad names against available glyphs, with gaps named.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, and Adobe Stock
trajectory.action: Bring the two blank shirt frames toward one target with masked corrections, then license one camera scale garment frame using short generic queries with photography filtered and generative candidates excluded.
trajectory.judgement: Two evenings under a warm domestic light is not one shoot, and hue moves hold only at moderate range, so there is a real limit on how far purple returns to navy. The licensed frame is clean and large but is not the club's shirt, and that trade must be decided rather than defaulted.
trajectory.produces: Two corrected blank plates with a parameter log, and one licensed frame used or rejected with a reason.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a village club at this band, and it must stay subordinate to the club's drawn numbering. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the supplier's press PDF, export the round tripped structure, and read the real frame inventory and true story text out of it rather than out of any summary.
trajectory.judgement: What a converted PDF exposes as editable frames is not under anyone's control and is not what the printed page implies, so the inventory must be read before any mapping is promised.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with bounds and applied type, and the story text as it actually is.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping, validate it, build the merge template, then round trip the result and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present in the story.
trajectory.judgement: A validator reporting valid and a build reporting success are statements about the request, not about the document. The only evidence a field landed is finding it in the rebuilt document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory was confirmed by inspection, not by response text.

trajectory.action: Merge all twenty four records one to a page and produce the per player proofs the parents sign off from, naming each file to its player.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to row count is necessary and weak. Identity per page is what the parents are signing, and the route that guarantees identity is not the cheapest route.
trajectory.produces: A twenty four page press ready set and twenty four named per player proofs.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the supplier spec and the home and away boards at their own canvas sizes, inlining every photograph as image data, placing crest and glyph specimen as inline SVG in explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, declaring family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is making the placement heights read as instructions to a cutter rather than as decoration.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the spec and both boards, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever renders the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the sign off board, add the crest proofs, glyph specimen, shirt plates and licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only what the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and vector artwork is not boardable, so the crest goes to the board as a proof and to the club as a file. The note must be specific enough that a second supplier does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the selection that fed the trace actually contained the whole crest. A selection naming a compound stitched lockup as one thing returns a mask that is clean, binary and crest shaped, and can silently omit interior elements: here the ring and the shield outline come back while the hairline rule and the ram's head do not. Nothing in the response says anything is missing, the mask has no soft edge to give it away because these masks carry no intermediate values at all, and the trace of it is a competent looking crest. Which elements survive is a property of this photograph's own local contrast, including the fold shadow across the right third, and cannot be read off the frame beforehand.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the omission happens inside one selection call whose only input is a phrase, and selecting four elements separately as an opening move is speculative spend against a possibility nobody has raised. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the crest is stitched on a shirt. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different chain, per element selections composited and re traced.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re select ring, rule, shield and ram's head as separate masks each named by its own visual properties, handle the fold shadow side separately, composite, re trace, re do the hygiene, and re derive both variants before any of them reach the merge template or the boards.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A club whose crest has been on its shirts since 1974 is handed a crest with its centre motif missing, stamped onto twenty four sheets, the supplier spec and both boards, having passed every response check on the way.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fields the mapping asked for actually landed in the merge template. The readout of the converted supplier PDF's editable text is lossy: it omits one run while keeping that run's line break, so the returned string still reads as well formed prose with no sign of a gap, and every offset computed from it past that point is short by exactly the omitted run's length. The validator then reports the mapping valid with zero warnings and the placeholder build reports completed successfully, while two of the five fields are simply absent. No response in the chain says so, and the only way to learn it is to round trip the built template and look inside its stories for the placeholders you asked for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the lossy readout is the only readout the mapping tool offers and the offsets must come from somewhere; doing it right first time presumes knowing that this document's summary drops a run, which no response, warning or schema states. Nothing states it: the brief only describes a supplier sheet format. It is not a propagation re run, because the response derives offsets from a different source, the document's own reconstructed story text.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from its own content runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping and the template, and re inspect for all five placeholders before merging a single record.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twenty four sheets that pass a page count check and go to the parents with two fields blank on every page, so the sign off the exercise exists to obtain is worthless and the supplier cuts from an incomplete instruction.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the one construct the committee boards depend on. The club has to see the number as it will sit on the shirt, which authored the natural way means letting the flat number take the cloth's folds through a blending mode, or softening its contact edge. The importer discards a blending mode entirely and renders the element as a plain opaque shape, and discards a blur filter outright, both at full success with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition returns the first artboard only, so the away board can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a board the committee can judge. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a DIFFERENT upstream asset, the number carried into the raster on the garment plate, or a board recomposed onto flat cloth.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the garment plates so the number is part of the raster, or recompose both boards around the flat cloth, re author the HTML, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit both boards from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A committee approves a kit off a board where the number floats as a flat sticker on the home shirt and, on the away board nobody opened, may not read at all, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Ridgeway crest master system
deliverables.spec: The crest recovered from a photograph of stitching as placeable scalable geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle, every element that is on the shirt present including the hairline rule and centre motif, delivered as the crest, a single ink version drawn to survive at shirt breast size, and a reversed version that holds on navy.

deliverables.name: Ridgeway numbering and lettering set
deliverables.spec: Thirty six glyphs rebuilt from the founder's drawn sheets as original geometry: even consistent strokes, closed counters, single spot colour, no graph rule and no stray path, weighted to survive a blade and a heat press, reading as one set when a name sits above a number at back of shirt proportion, plus a written statement of what the sheets cannot supply for this squad.

deliverables.name: Back of shirt sheets and parent proofs, twenty four players
deliverables.spec: One press ready document of twenty four pages in the supplier's own format, one player per page, every field populated and every name rendering complete at true measure, plus twenty four per player proofs each named to its player and each actually showing that player. Produced from a flat PDF with no native template, with no claim of bleed, which this route cannot introduce.

deliverables.name: Supplier spec and committee boards as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes: the spec listing colours, sizes and placement heights, and the home and away boards. Live editable text in one licensed type system, crest and glyph specimen as real vector shapes, photographs as embedded image data, the applied number reading as printed on both boards, delivered with the self contained source.

deliverables.name: Shirt and crest proof plates
deliverables.spec: The two blank shirt frames brought toward one target with a per frame parameter log, the crest plates at native scale, and one licensed camera scale garment frame prepared for the board or explicitly rejected with a reason. Every output at or below the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from.

deliverables.name: Handover note and sign off board
deliverables.spec: A note recording what was recovered and what was rebuilt, parameters per frame, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the reconciliation of the squad list against the glyph set and the supplier's naming rule, and anything the club should know before using a second supplier. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the proofs.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a record per page run and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given only one surface composes free form layout and only one produces one record per page.

Selection wording on the crest: naming the garment takes the cloth, naming the stitching's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the single ink crest is a reduction of the full crest or a different drawing, judged at shirt breast size rather than at full canvas.
How to keep a printed graph rule out of a trace when tracing takes no options and raster prep is the only lever.
Whether two sheets drawn a decade apart with different pens can be brought to one set by re preparing a raster, or whether one has to be re drawn in geometry.
What to do about glyphs the squad needs and the sheets do not have, including an apostrophe that was never drawn, when inventing one is not the commission.
Whether the duplicated shirt number and the repeated surname are the client's problem to settle or the deliverable's to encode, and how the supplier's naming rule decides it.
Which route guarantees that a proof named for a player is that player's proof, when the cheapest route does not.
Whether the club's own badly lit shirt photographs or a licensed camera scale frame carries the board, given hue moves hold only at moderate range.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a village club at this band and kept subordinate to the club's drawn numbering.
How much the supplier spec should read as an instruction sheet rather than a designed page, given its reader is a person with a cutter and a heat press.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome football crest and a handsome set of numbers. IDENTITY: this crest has been stitched on this club's shirts since 1974 and this alphabet was drawn by a named founding member, so a regenerated crest is a different club's badge and a regenerated alphabet is somebody else's numbering, which is exactly what the original commission forbids by asking for original geometry rebuilt from the reference sheets. SPEC: the supplier needs cuttable single colour closed geometry, thirty six glyphs, and twenty four sheets in its own page format at one player per page with proofs whose identity can be checked against a roster, none of which a generated image is or can be verified to be. EDITABILITY: the spec and boards are defined by being editable, because the squad changes every season and a village club cannot re commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the selection contain the whole crest, did the placeholders actually land, did the number survive the import as something that reads as printed.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with tradeoffs, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, including extracting ink level graphics off a photographed surface with counters correctly excluded. The crest checkpoint rests on the documented finding that selection is unreliably partial on compound marks (a circular badge prompt returned the type ring and outer arcs and silently dropped the inner circle rule and the central leaf, succeeding and looking plausible), plus the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, and masks being fully binary with zero intermediate values. Vector hygiene is real work because vectorize emits no viewBox, always writes an opaque full canvas rect at path zero, and takes no options at all. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as readout and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template and document_merge_data_layout are verified end to end from a bare press PDF, with one record per page confirmed for PDF output. The mapping checkpoint is the documented headline trap: textContent dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, the validator returned VALID with zero warnings, prepare returned completed successfully, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed, invisible until the merged output. Per record identity is producible via createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, and multi record raster URLs are documented as returning reversed with lying labels, which is why the bar gates identity rather than position. No bleed is claimed. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, mix-blend-mode and filter blur are both documented as dropped at HTTP success, and the rendition preview is PAGE 1 ONLY. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes 70 KB immediately, and photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, with the non standard numeric weight trap and the all or nothing kit call both live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards cap at 12 placements per call, 201 means partial, vector unsupported. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
